m1, m2, ….,mn at positions (x1,y1), (x2,y2) , 0,…,(xn,yn)
respectively. Consider F1, F2 ,…, Fn be the forces
applied to the individual particles m1, m2, ….,mn so
that they produce acceleration a1,a2,…,an.
One writes, F1+F2+…+Fn = m1a1+ m2a2+…+ mnan
Or, ∑F = m1 d2x1/dt2 + m2d2x2/dt2+…+ mnd2xn/dt2
= d2/dt2 (m1x1+ m2x2+…+ mnxn)
Or, ∑F ∑m = d2/dt2 [m1 x1+m2 x2+⋯…+mnxn (m1+m2+⋯.+mn) ]

For (X, Y) to be the point of center of mass, we concluded from above ; X = m1 x1 +m2 x2+⋯…+mnxn (m1 +m2 +⋯.+mn)
And, Y = m1 y1 +m2 y2 +⋯…+mnyn (m1 +m2 +⋯.+mn)
Therefore, the point of center,
(X, Y) = (m1 x1+m2 x2 +⋯…+mnxn , m1 y1 +m2 y2 +⋯…+mnyn)
For a two-body system of masses m1 and m2 as shown, let P be the point of center of mass at
positions x1 and x2 respectively from the bodies.
Then, we write, m1x1 = m2x2 ∴ x1 = m2 x2 m1 and x2 = m1 x1 m2
The position of the centre of mass determines the position of the centre of gravity.
Hence the greater the mass, the nearer is the position of the center of gravity.
Worked Out Examples: Q: Two particles of masses 1kg and 2kg are located at x=0 and x =3 m. Find the position of the centre of mass.

Solution: The centre of mass clearly lies between the particles on the positive X-axis. Let r1 = x be the position of the centre of mass from the particle of 1 kg mass and hence r2 =3-x be the position of the centre of mass from the particle of 2kg mass. Now from m1r1 = m2r2,
1. x = 2(3-x)⇒x = 2cm Hence the centre of mass lies at 2cm from the origin.

Center of Gravity: It is the point through which the resultant weight of the body is supposed to be acting vertically downwards. The center of gravity of an object is a geometric property representing the average location of the body's weight. The center of gravity (C.G) may or may not lie within the body. For a spherical or disk-like body, it lies at the center within the material of

the body. However, for a ring or spherical enclosure, the C.G also lies at the center but not within the material of the body. The center of gravity is used in designing static structures such as buildings, bridges, flying airplanes, kites, etc. If the center of gravity lies in the middle and at a lower position, it provides more stability to the structure.

Activity 7.1 Do the activities that follows i) Take a long, uniform bar and support it horizontally at the tips of two fingers to keep the bar level. ii) Take a circular disc, square, rectangular, or triangular lamina. Support it on a tip of a needle towards the center point of the body. iii) Find the position of the center of gravity for each item taken. Clearly, the center of gravity is the point where, when the body is supported on it, the body remains in equilibrium.

The shapes of the bodies and position of C.G for the various bodies are listed below: i) The uniform bar (rod) → Center point ii) Disc or Circular ring → Center point iii) Sphere body and Angular disc → At the Center iv) Triangular lamina → Point of interstion of the medians v) Rectangle or Cubical block → Point of interstion of the diagonals vi) Square, Rectangular or Parallelogram like lamina → Point of interstion of the diagonals vii) Cylinder → Middle point of axis viii) Cone of Pyramid → on the line joining the center to the base at a distance equal to 1 of the length of the line from the base.

Hence for the stability (equilibrium of a body), the base of the body should be as wide as possible. i.) The bottom of the ship is made heavier for this reason. The addition of cargo enforces the center of equilibrium to lie at the lowest position, thereby producing more stability. ii) A double - decker bus may easily topple over as there is shift of center of gravity upwards due to the passenger’s weight. iii) The boat loses its balance when passengers stand on it due to the upward shift of the center of gravity.
